dish: White chai tow kway (pan-fried radish cake)
address: Toa Payoh West Market & Food Centre, #02-30, Blk 127 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, S310127
w: Michelin Bib Gourmand since 2016 — two sisters fry each plate of crispy-yet-spongy white carrot cake to order, drawing long queues at the freshly renovated (reopened Aug 2025) Toa Payoh West hawker centre.

dish: Wok-fried Hokkien prawn mee in reduced prawn stock
n: Come Daily Fried Hokkien Prawn Mee
address: Toa Payoh West Market & Food Centre, #02-27, Blk 127 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, S310127
w: Michelin-listed and running since 1968, Steven Ng reduces prawn stock right in the wok for one of Toa Payoh's most famous plates of Hokkien mee — a fixture of the reopened Toa Payoh West food centre.

dish: Old-school Hainanese beef noodles with tendon, tripe & beef balls
n: Hai Nan Xing Zhou Beef Noodle
address: Kim Keat Palm Market & Food Centre, #01-06, Blk 22 Lorong 7 Toa Payoh, S310022
w: Nearly 70 years of Hainanese beef noodles from S$5, newly awarded a Michelin Bib Gourmand — dry or soup, in a rich braise the whole hawker centre queues for.

dish: $5 wanton mee with overnight-marinated char siew
address: Block A, Jackson Square, 11 Toa Payoh Lorong 3, S319579
w: A Michelin-starred Cantonese chef sells $5 wanton mee from a warehouse-canteen stall — HK-shipped springy noodles and charred char siew that earned a Michelin Bib Gourmand within a year of opening (still listed 2025/2026).

dish: Teochew mee pok with handmade yellowtail fishballs
address: Kim Keat Palm Market & Food Centre, #01-20, Blk 22 Lorong 7 Toa Payoh, S310022
w: The original stall of Singapore's 58-year-old fishball dynasty (est. 1968), Michelin Bib Gourmand for four years running since 2022 — springy, umami yellowtail fishballs made fresh daily.

dish: $1 nasi lemak (coconut rice, ikan bilis/kuning fish, egg, sambal)
address: Blk 20 Toa Payoh Lorong 7 coffeeshop, S310020
w: A beloved $1 nasi lemak that has held its price since 1987 to stay affordable for elderly regulars — cooking starts at 4am and 300-500 plates sell out by midday; covered by every major food outlet and YouTuber Ghib Ojisan.

dish: Fried chicken wing Hainanese chicken rice
address: Toa Payoh Lorong 5 Food Centre, #01-31, Blk 75 Lorong 5 Toa Payoh, S310075
w: A cult chicken rice stall that swaps roast/poached chicken for addictively marinated crispy fried wings ($3.50) with a spicy chilli dip — famously long evening queues until sold out.

dish: Handmade yellowtail fishball & minced-meat noodles
address: Blk 22 Lorong 7 Toa Payoh, #01-58, S310022
w: The Toa Payoh outlet of Uncle David Ng's famed noodle stall, where bouncy yellowtail fishballs are hand-pounded on the spot (the Holland Drive original holds the Michelin Bib Gourmand).

dish: Hokkien-style popiah & kueh pie tee (recipe since 1930)
address: Kim Keat Palm Market & Food Centre, #01-03, Blk 22 Lorong 7 Toa Payoh, S310022
w: A 3rd-generation popiah stall with roots to 1930, hand-rolling Hokkien-style popiah (no pork, no lard, no MSG) with house-fried sole-fish crisps — one of Singapore's most heritage popiah names.

dish: Bak chor mee (minced-pork mushroom noodles) & kway teow soup
n: Lai Heng Mushroom Minced Meat Noodle
address: Blk 73 Toa Payoh Lorong 5, Toa Payoh
w: A bak chor mee institution running since 1985 (relocated twice within Toa Payoh), still turning out a spicy dry mee kia and a standout lard-rich kway teow soup that Seth Lui rated after 24 years of visits.

dish: Caramel-crusted 'ugly' muffins (chocolate, blueberry, mushroom-herb)
address: Toa Payoh West Market & Food Centre, #02-34, Blk 127 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, S310127
w: UK-trained ex-engineer Anton Tan turned his family's zi char stall into a viral $1.20 muffin institution — deliberately misshapen buns with crunchy caramelised crusts; a long-queue hawker-dessert cult reopened after the 2025 renovation.

dish: Handmade Teochew pau (lotus paste, char siew) & siew mai
address: Toa Payoh West Market & Food Centre, Blk 127 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, S310127
w: A 30-plus-year heritage pau stall (est. 1993, three years on the Michelin Plate) hand-making Teochew-style buns with thick, not-too-sweet lotus paste — announced closure end-2025 but reopened June 2026 after public demand.

dish: Hakka lei cha (thunder tea rice) with crispy add-ons
address: Toa Payoh West Market & Food Centre, Blk 127 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, S310127
w: Two sisters plate one of Singapore's most generous $5 thunder tea rice sets — less oil, less salt, no MSG — with the fragrant bitter-green tea broth poured over brown rice and crunchy toppings.

dish: Silky tau huay (soya beancurd) & thick soya milk
address: Toa Payoh West Market & Food Centre, Blk 127 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, S310127
w: Ex-Italian-restaurant cook Desheng makes beancurd from scratch daily with non-GMO soybeans — smooth, un-gritty tau huay you can dress with gula melaka, grass jelly or gingko.

dish: Hainanese scissor-cut curry rice
n: Toa Payoh Scissors Cut Curry Rice
address: Toa Payoh Lorong 8 Market & Food Centre, 210 Lorong 8 Toa Payoh, S310210
w: Old-school Hainanese-style curry rice from S$2.80 — a heaped plate of chopped sides flooded in three different gravies (curry, braise, pork), a comfort-food fixture of Lorong 8.

dish: Scallop glutinous rice (lor mai kai) & Hong Kong dim sum
n: Uncle Kun's Delicacies (Kun Shu Food Stall)
address: Toa Payoh Vista Market, Lorong 4 Toa Payoh
w: Ex-hotel HK chef Lam Kun serves restaurant-grade dim sum at hawker prices; his signature oblong scallop glutinous rice (S$4.80), packed with dried scallop, salted egg and lap cheong, isn't found elsewhere in Singapore.

dish: $3.50 wanton mee with soupy & fried wantons
n: Min Kee Tanjong Rhu Wanton Noodle
address: Kim Keat Palm Market & Food Centre, Blk 22 Lorong 7 Toa Payoh, S310022
w: A decades-old wanton mee that relocated from Tanjong Rhu, still selling a substantial $3.50 bowl of springy noodles with black-chilli option, soupy and fried wantons — a Kim Keat breakfast favourite.

dish: Handmade muah chee (peanut / black sesame)
address: Gourmet Paradise Food Court, Toa Payoh HDB Hub, Blk 480 Lorong 6 Toa Payoh, #B1-01, S310480
w: Likely the last hawker hand-making this Teochew snack from scratch — Teo Yong Joo mills flour, roasts peanuts and pinches each soft, tender muah chee ball to order at the HDB Hub food court.

dish: Claypot Hokkien mee with crispy sio bak
address: Blk 92 Toa Payoh Lorong 4, #01-264, S310092
w: Once rated among Singapore's top-five Hokkien mee — served in a heat-retaining claypot with deep-fried crispy pork belly — this 10-year Toa Payoh favourite shuttered on 28 Feb 2026. Kept here as a flagged closure.

dish: Handmade Hakka yong tau foo (fried fish paste, stuffed tofu)
n: Hup Chong Hakka Yong Tau Foo — CLOSED
address: Blk 203 Toa Payoh (final location; earlier Blk 116/124)
w: A four-generation Hakka yong tau foo with roots to a 1952 pushcart, famous for handmade fried meatballs and fish paste — it closed for good on 28 Jan 2026 after 70-plus years amid falling footfall. Kept here as a flagged closure.
